phases.name: Control plane and housekeeping
phases.objective: Establish one enforced plan, a clean baseline, and protected repository governance.
phases.exitCriteria: All PH0 release blockers are complete and every later item has an owner, dependency chain, acceptance criteria, and evidence requirement.

phases.name: Security boundary
phases.objective: Close known navigation, IPC, command invocation, approval, and lifecycle defects.
phases.exitCriteria: All known exploitable boundary defects are fixed, regression-tested, reviewed by a separate verifier agent, and reflected in the threat model.

phases.name: Runtime contract
phases.objective: Make sandbox enforcement and Codex compatibility explicit, bounded, and testable.
phases.exitCriteria: Unsupported or unsafe runtime states fail closed and every supported Codex version passes schema and real-flow tests.

phases.name: Verification system
phases.objective: Build automated proof for application boundaries, behavior, accessibility, and supported environments.
phases.exitCriteria: Security-critical flows run in real Electron and the clean-machine matrix is automated or has a controlled evidence procedure.

phases.name: Supply chain and deterministic build
phases.objective: Lock, record, reproduce, inspect, attest, and verify every released artifact.
phases.exitCriteria: Build inputs are immutable or recorded, package policy passes, and independent rebuild comparison is repeatable.

phases.name: Release qualification
phases.objective: Qualify one release candidate across the entire supported matrix and operational lifecycle.
phases.exitCriteria: The release-candidate commit passes every security, compatibility, package, privacy, legal, update, rollback, and support gate.

phases.name: Stable release and operations
phases.objective: Publish the already-qualified artifact and operate a sustainable vulnerability and update process.
phases.exitCriteria: Stable artifacts are verifiable, monitoring and response ownership are active, and a post-release review is recorded.

workItems.title: Establish the canonical machine-validated readiness ledger
acceptanceCriteria: A single ledger defines phases, ownership, dependencies, status, acceptance, and evidence
A validator runs as part of npm run verify
Stable version declaration fails while release blockers remain incomplete
independenceLimitations: One human authority; agent roles do not constitute independent-human review
residualRisks: A compromised or unavailable sole-owner account can alter or halt governance

workItems.title: Reconcile the local branch, untracked handoff, and open dependency pull requests
acceptanceCriteria: The intended local commit is reviewed and pushed through a pull request or documented protected-branch exception
HANDOFF.md is deliberately committed, relocated, or removed without losing useful state
Pull request 6 is closed or replaced with compatible updates
Pull requests 7 and 8 are reviewed, tested, and resolved without weakening action pinning policy
git status is clean at the baseline commit

workItems.title: Enforce repository, branch, tag, and vulnerability-reporting governance
acceptanceCriteria: main requires pull requests, required CI, resolved conversations, and prevents force-push and deletion
Release tags are protected from mutation and deletion
Private vulnerability reporting is enabled and tested
Release publication uses an approval-protected environment
Sole-owner account recovery, succession, archival, and security-response limitations are documented

workItems.title: Create issue and pull-request traceability for every readiness item
acceptanceCriteria: Every non-complete ledger item links to one tracking issue
Issue templates require work-item ID, acceptance criteria, dependencies, test plan, and evidence
Pull-request templates prohibit completing items without ledger and evidence updates

workItems.title: Enforce allowlists across navigation, redirects, windows, and external links
acceptanceCriteria: will-navigate and will-redirect enforce the same centralized allowlist
Programmatic and server redirects cannot escape trusted destinations
Only deliberately allowed HTTPS links reach the system browser
Regression tests cover subdomain, lookalike, encoded, redirect-chain, and non-HTTPS cases

workItems.title: Bind privileged IPC to an immutable trusted renderer origin
acceptanceCriteria: Packaged builds ignore ELECTRON_RENDERER_URL
Development renderer URLs are restricted to configured loopback origins
Every privileged IPC request verifies WebContents, main frame, and exact renderer origin
A remote or redirected document cannot inherit the privileged preload bridge

workItems.title: Constrain and validate the renderer-to-Codex RPC surface
acceptanceCriteria: Renderer-callable app-server methods are explicitly allowlisted
Security-sensitive request payloads are schema-validated and fail closed
API-key and injected-token login remain prohibited
Unknown methods and malformed payloads have negative tests

workItems.title: Eliminate plugin marketplace argument injection and unsafe source ambiguity
acceptanceCriteria: Marketplace sources cannot be interpreted as CLI options
Sources are validated as an approved URL form or absolute local path
Installation shows source and capability-impact confirmation
Adversarial names and sources are covered by tests

workItems.title: Correct approval decisions and make consent understandable
acceptanceCriteria: Legacy and current allow, deny, abort, and timeout responses match generated protocol types
Approval UI identifies command, working directory, network impact, and file changes
Malformed, duplicate, expired, and replayed approval responses fail closed
Real Codex approval allow and deny flows pass end to end

workItems.title: Bound RPC lifetime, restart concurrency, and child-process resource use
acceptanceCriteria: All UI and router requests have defined timeouts and bounded pending state
Disconnect and restart reject outstanding work with actionable errors
Only one restart executes at a time and crash loops are rate-limited
Plugin and child-process invocation has concurrency and resource limits

workItems.title: Make Linux sandbox availability an active fail-closed runtime gate
acceptanceCriteria: Smoke testing fails when bubblewrap or user-namespace isolation is unavailable
Late sandbox warnings cannot leave the UI in a ready state
Supported AppArmor and user-namespace configurations pass an active safe probe
No production no-sandbox fallback exists

workItems.title: Define and enforce a finite supported Codex CLI contract
acceptanceCriteria: The project records a reviewed decision to bundle a permitted version or support a finite minimum and maximum range
Unknown older and newer versions are rejected with remediation guidance
Every supported version passes initialization, OAuth, turn, approval, interrupt, restart, plugin, and logout tests
Experimental app-server risk and upgrade cadence are documented

workItems.title: Control generated Codex schemas and protocol drift
acceptanceCriteria: Generated schemas carry generator version, source version, command, and digest provenance
CI regeneration detects unexplained schema drift
Schema changes require protocol and security review
The checked-in schema set matches every supported CLI contract

workItems.title: Build a real Electron security and critical-flow end-to-end suite
acceptanceCriteria: Tests execute the packaged Electron boundary rather than only jsdom and unit mocks
Navigation, redirect, popup, IPC, preload, permission, download, and renderer-crash cases are covered
OAuth, thread, turn, approval, interrupt, restart, plugin, logout, and remote-view failure cases are covered
Security-critical tests are required checks

workItems.title: Automate or strictly control the clean-machine compatibility matrix
acceptanceCriteria: Ubuntu, Debian, and Fedora versions have pinned test images or recorded clean-VM definitions
X11, Wayland, x64, ARM64, DEB, and RPM cells are individually tracked
Install, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, ownership, desktop integration, AppArmor, and sandbox behavior are verified
Unsupported or untested matrix cells cannot produce advertised artifacts

workItems.title: Add protocol robustness, fuzz, stress, and coverage gates
acceptanceCriteria: JSONL framing, malformed records, size limits, reordering, and cancellation receive property or fuzz coverage
Reconnect and restart stress tests demonstrate bounded memory and pending state
Security-critical modules have an enforced branch-coverage threshold

workItems.title: Establish accessibility and failure-recovery acceptance tests
acceptanceCriteria: Keyboard, focus, screen-reader labels, scaling, and high-contrast behavior pass documented criteria
Renderer crash, app-server crash, network failure, login expiry, and remote-load failure recover safely
Approval dialogs remain understandable and operable without a pointer

workItems.title: Pin and minimize all build and workflow inputs
acceptanceCriteria: GitHub Actions use reviewed full commit SHAs
Runner, container, Node, npm, Electron, packager, system package, locale, timezone, and architecture inputs are pinned or captured
Workflow permissions are least privilege per job and publishing cannot execute from pull requests
Caches cannot change output and release builds start from ephemeral environments

workItems.title: Resolve build-chain vulnerabilities and remove unused production surface
acceptanceCriteria: DR-001 is closed by a fixed dependency graph or independently accepted for a short explicit period
No unresolved high or critical runtime vulnerability exists
Unused runtime dependencies and unsupported packaged bridge code are removed
Node engine and type definitions match the tested minimum runtime

workItems.title: Make DEB and RPM installation policy-correct and sandbox-safe
acceptanceCriteria: AppArmor installation precedes final sandbox capability selection and does not leave unnecessary setuid state
Installed ownership, permissions, dependencies, desktop metadata, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall pass policy checks
Every Electron fuse is named, explicitly configured, and asserted with a compatible verifier
DEB and RPM install required copyright, license, notice, and privacy material
The desktop entry does not advertise unsupported URL handling

workItems.title: Produce artifact-content SBOMs, checksums, provenance, and consumer verification
acceptanceCriteria: SBOM generation inventories each final DEB and RPM rather than only the npm dependency graph
Checksums and provenance identify the exact published artifacts
CI verifies attestations and SBOM correspondence before publication
Users have tested checksum and attestation verification instructions

workItems.title: Implement independent deterministic rebuild comparison
acceptanceCriteria: Unsigned DEB and RPM artifacts are built twice in isolated environments from the same declared inputs
Byte equality is tested with cryptographic digests
Time, path, locale, timezone, username, filesystem ordering, and cache variance are exercised
Any unavoidable normalization is scripted, minimal, reviewed, and documented
A separate verifier-agent run reproduces and compares artifacts, with limitations disclosed to the owner

workItems.title: Minimize remote-data activity and provide complete local-data control
acceptanceCriteria: ChatGPT network and persistent session creation are lazy and user-initiated
Logout and clear-local-data controls cover ChatGPT and documented Codex state
Privacy documentation names exact data paths, retention, cleanup, uninstall residue, and diagnostic redaction
Network behavior and cleanup are verified on every supported distro

workItems.title: Define update, rollback, support, and vulnerability-response operations
acceptanceCriteria: Users receive authenticated security-update notification or a supported updater path
Rollback retains and verifies the previous supported artifact
Security severity, response targets, disclosure, patch, and end-of-life processes are documented
A vulnerability-report tabletop exercise and update rollback drill pass

workItems.title: Complete legal, trademark, licensing, and redistribution review
acceptanceCriteria: Third-party notices and package license inventories are complete
ChatGPT embedding, Codex integration or bundling decision, OpenAI marks, disclaimers, and distribution terms receive recorded owner or counsel review
The Apache-2.0 warranty disclaimer and support expectations are clearly presented
No unsupported affiliation or security certification claim appears in product or release material

workItems.title: Qualify one immutable release candidate across the supported matrix
acceptanceCriteria: One commit and candidate version pass verify, full audits, CodeQL, dependency review, Electron end-to-end, Codex compatibility, and every advertised matrix cell
The candidate tag, package version, changelog, schema manifest, SBOM, provenance, and checksums agree
No artifact is rebuilt between qualification and publication
A separate verifier-agent report and two explicit sole-owner release decisions are retained without claiming independent-human review

workItems.title: Publish the qualified stable artifacts without rebuilding
acceptanceCriteria: Publication promotes the exact qualified artifact digests
Stable publication requires protected-tag and protected-environment approval
Release notes state support matrix, known limitations, verification steps, privacy cleanup, rollback, and security reporting
A clean consumer machine verifies and installs the published artifact

workItems.title: Operate recurring dependency, platform, incident, and release reviews
acceptanceCriteria: Electron, Codex, Node, builder, distro, and dependency support reviews have named cadence and owner
Vulnerability intake and update delivery metrics are reviewed after each release
A post-release review records incidents, user-impacting defects, drift, and corrective work
The plan is re-baselined through reviewed ledger changes rather than silent status edits
